additions.node_text: רְשָׁעִים הַמְזַמְּרִים נִגּוּנִים שֶׁל יְלָלָה וְעַצְבוּת
additions.reason: The wicked who sing melodies of wailing and sadness are explicitly declared a bechina of the souls of the Erev Rav ('הֵם בְּחִינַת נִשְׁמַת עֵרֶב רַב'). This is the opening bechina statement of the Torah. They belong to the evil cluster of corrupted sight and Lilit's domain — their wailing songs ARE the expression of Lilit's constant wailing (as their mother/source). Proposed package: new evil package (see torah_226_new_packages.json).
additions.source_quote: מַה שֶּׁהָרְשָׁעִים עַל פִּי רֹב הֵם מְזַמְּרִים נִגּוּנִים שֶׁל יְלָלָה וְעַצְבוּת, כִּי הֵם בְּחִינַת נִשְׁמַת עֵרֶב רַב

additions.reason: The souls of the Erev Rav (mixed multitude) are the bechina peer of the wicked who sing wailing melodies. They belong to the evil cluster. Their mother is Lilit, who constantly wails — meaning the Erev Rav souls share Lilit's wailing essence. This is the second node in the opening bechina equation. Proposed package: new evil package (see torah_226_new_packages.json).
additions.source_quote: הֵם בְּחִינַת נִשְׁמַת עֵרֶב רַב, וְאִמָּא דְּעֵרֶב רַב הִיא לִילִית שֶׁהִיא מְיַלֶּלֶת תָּמִיד

additions.reason: Lilit is identified as the mother (אִמָּא) of the Erev Rav — she shares their essential nature as the wailing, corrupting, dark force. She is also identified with the defective spelling of מְאֹרֹת (luminaries written without the vav, חָסֵר) via Tikunei Zohar. She is the dominant node of the evil cluster: both the wailing melodies of the wicked and the corruption of sight trace back to her as their root. Proposed package: new evil package (see torah_226_new_packages.json).
additions.source_quote: אִמָּא דְּעֵרֶב רַב הִיא לִילִית שֶׁהִיא מְיַלֶּלֶת תָּמִיד

additions.reason: The soft eyes of Leah (Genesis 29:17) are identified as a bechina of the corruption of sight ('יְנִיקָתָם מִבְּחִינַת: וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת... מִבְּחִינַת קִלְקוּל הָרְאוּת'). This is explicit bechina language. The 'soft eyes' represent the weakened, corrupted state of vision that is Lilit's domain (defective Meoros). The concept has a dual aspect — it is also the source from which Shevet Levi draws, giving melody its power — but in this Torah it primarily anchors the evil/defective side. Polarity: evil in the context of this Torah's evil cluster. Proposed package: new evil package.
additions.source_quote: יְנִיקָתָם מִבְּחִינַת: וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת (בראשית כ״ט:י״ז), מִבְּחִינַת קִלְקוּל הָרְאוּת

additions.reason: The corruption of sight is the evil mirror of Package 1's 'תִּקּוּן הָרְאוּת בִּשְׁלֵמוּת'. It is stated as the bechina of ועיני לאה רכות, and is the spiritual mechanism by which evil melodies attract people: their sustenance (יניקה) comes from this corrupted sight-domain. It is the central concept linking the wailing melodies, Leah's eyes, and Lilit. Proposed package: new evil package.
additions.source_quote: יְנִיקָתָם מִבְּחִינַת: וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת, מִבְּחִינַת קִלְקוּל הָרְאוּת

additions.reason: The word מְאֹרֹת (luminaries) written defectively (without a vav, חָסֵר) in Genesis 1 is equated with Lilit by Tikunei Zohar (Tikun 44, p. 79b), and the Rebbe quotes this equation explicitly: 'בִּבְחִינַת מְאֹרֹת חָסֵר — דָּא לִילִית'. Defective Meoros = Lilit. This is a bechina of the corrupted light/sight domain. The vav-deficient spelling represents incomplete, diminished light — exactly the corruption of sight that is Lilit's province. Proposed package: new evil package.
additions.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת מְאֹרֹת חָסֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שם א): יְהִי מְאֹרֹת – חָסֵר, דָּא לִילִית (ת"ז תיקון מד דף עט:)

additions.reason: Shevet Levi (the tribe of Levi) is identified as the 'side of melody' (סִטְרָא דְּנִגּוּנָא) per the Zohar (Shemos p. 19). They directed the Temple songs. Levi is from Leah's children — he originates in the same source (Leah's eyes) as the corrupted melodies, yet he is the holy side of music. This dual origin makes Levi/melody a neutral structural concept: the same musical domain can be holy (Shevet Levi's sacred song) or evil (wailing melodies of the Erev Rav). His name derives from 'יִלָּוֶה' (he will draw/attach) — the drawing power of melody. Proposed package: new neutral melody package (see torah_226_new_packages.json).

additions.reason: The 'side of melody' (Zohar Shemos p. 19) is explicitly equated with Levi: 'לֵוִי שֶׁהוּא סִטְרָא דְּנִגּוּנָא'. This is a bechina statement — Levi IS the melody-dimension. Together with שֵׁבֶט לֵוִי and the concept of יִלָּוֶה (drawing/attaching through melody), this forms a neutral cluster: the structural domain of music that can go either toward holiness or toward evil. Proposed package: new neutral melody package.

analysis_notes.torah_structure_note: Torah #226 is a brief but conceptually rich teaching with a clear good/evil mirror structure. The evil pole (wailing melodies ← Erev Rav souls ← Lilit ← defective Meoros ← corrupted sight ← Leah's soft eyes) mirrors the good pole (Shabbat = complete repair of sight). The medial/neutral domain is melody itself (Shevet Levi / sitra d'niguna), which originates from the same source as the evil melodies (Leah's children) but represents the holy musical dimension. On Shabbat, the holy power of complete sight elevates even the evil melodies — the Torah's practical teaching. The dataset captures only ONE of the Torah's bechina equations (Shabbat ↔ tikkun harei'ut), leaving the entire evil cluster and the melody cluster unencoded.
analysis_notes.encoding_priority: High. The evil cluster (לילית / ערב רב / קלקול הראות / מאורות חסר / עיני לאה רכות) is conceptually rich and appears in multiple Torahs. Lilit and Erev Rav are significant recurring concepts. The melody cluster (שבט לוי / סטרא דניגונא) is referenced from Zohar and is distinctive. Both clusters should be added to torahData.js.
